title: Scanning electron microscopy of murine skin ultrathin sections and cultured keratinocytes
protocol: Wash fixed samples three times for 5 minutes each with 0.1M Na-Cacodylate buffer (pH 7.2) at room temperature on a rotor.
Post-fix samples with 1% Osmium Tetroxide in 0.1M Na-Cacodylate buffer (pH 7.2) for 3–4 hours on ice, agitating gently from time to time or using a rotor.
Wash samples three times successively with 0.1M Na-Cacodylate buffer (pH 7.2).
Wash samples four times for 5 minutes each with 0.05M Maleate buffer (pH 5.2).
Stain samples with Uranyl Acetate (UA) in 1% UA solution in 0.05M Maleate buffer (pH 5.2) for 1.5 hours at room temperature in the dark.
Fill at least half the scintillation vial volume with dehydration solvent.
Invert the vial gently several times to remove any sample and water from the lid.
Incubate samples in 30% ethanol for 15 minutes with rotation at 4°C.
Incubate samples in 50% ethanol for 15 minutes with rotation at 4°C.
Incubate samples in 70% ethanol for 15 minutes with rotation at 4°C.
Store samples overnight in 70% ethanol at 4°C if necessary.
Incubate samples in 95% ethanol for 15 minutes with rotation at room temperature (RT).
Incubate samples in 100% ethanol three times, each for 10 minutes with rotation at RT.
Infiltrate the dehydrated samples with EPON resin embedding solution.
Prepare EPON resin as described.
Mix 100% propylene oxide: EPON resin (2:1) and incubate sample for 2 hours at RT with gentle agitation in a scintillation vial.
Incubate the sample in a vial containing 100% Propylene oxide: EPON resin (1:1) for 2 h at RT with gentle agitation.
Remove the sample from the 1:1 mixture and incubate it in a new vial containing 100% Propylene oxide: EPON resin (1:2) for 2 h at RT with gentle agitation.
Remove the sample from the 1:2 mixture and incubate it in a new vial containing 100% EPON resin for 6 h at RT with gentle agitation.
Continue the incubation with fresh 100% EPON resin for at least another 6 h with agitation.
Embed the sample in silicone molds by filling half the mold with resin and curing it at 60°C overnight.
Place the sample in an orientation in the previously prepared EPON resin bed inside the mold.
Fill the rest of the mold with fresh EPON resin.
Avoid bubbles during filling to ensure stability of the sample position.
Leave the EPON resin to polymerize for 48 hours at 60°C.
Trim away excess surface resin using a single-edge razor until the skin sample can be seen.
Use a razor blade to trim the top of the mold into a trapezium block shape with sloping sides.
Ensure that the top and bottom of the trapezium shape are parallel to each other, with the bottom being longer than the top.
Make final adjustments to the trapezoid by trimming away as much excess resin as possible.
Place and secure the chuck containing the trimmed resin onto the cantilever arm of the ultramicrotome.
Place a freshly prepared glass knife onto the knife holder.
Prepare two knives from one glass square using a Leica EM KMR3 glass knife maker.
Store the knives in a knife holder box to prevent dust collection on their edges.
Orient the EPON resin block/glass knife such that the longer side of the trapezoid is parallel to the knife-edge.
Move the block away from the knife-edge during alignment to protect both surfaces from damage.
Trim the surface of the trapezoid block until it becomes completely flat with a mirror-like quality.
Prepare a fresh glass knife.
Attach a plastic boat to the glass knife using wax.
Test for leakage by filling with water and ensuring no leaks occur.
Dry the setup for at least 30 minutes after testing.
Replace the existing glass or diamond knife on the ultramicrotome.
Move the block away from the knife-edge during replacement.
Set the clearance angle of the knife to 6°.
Fill the plastic boat with deionized water using a 1 mL syringe.
Adjust the water level in the boat so that it reaches the knife-edge.
Maintain the correct water level to ensure uniform section thickness.
Orient the EPON resin block such that its longer side is parallel to the knife-edge.
Carefully bring the block to the knife-edge, leaving a gap of 3–4 mm between the block and the knife-edge.
Make finer adjustments to the alignment between the longer side of the trapezoid and the knife-edge by specimen rotation alignment.
Adjust the alignment by knife lateral alignment.
Tilt the knife for better alignment.
Tilt the specimen for optimal alignment.
From the block face, section 500 nm–1 μm sections.
Stain with toluidine blue.
Examine under a light microscope.
Trim the block face even smaller which contains only the ROI.
Switch to a diamond knife or a freshly prepared glass knife for further sectioning.
Set the cutting window on an automated ultramicrotome by defining the top position (specimen block 1 cm above the knife-edge) and the bottom position (specimen block 1 cm below the knife-edge).
Set the sectioning speed from 0.5 mm/s to 1.0 mm/s.
Adjust the section thickness from semi-thin (100nm–120 nm) to ultra-thin (60 nm) depending on the desired imaging technique (SEM vs TEM).
Stain with toluidine blue to focus on the correct ROI and sample orientation.
Determine section thickness using an interference card that provides a color spectrum reflecting its respective section thickness.
Use an eyelash brush to detach sections from the knife-edge.
Guide the sections towards the end of the boat using the eyelash brush for easier collection.
Flatten the sections with isopropanol vapors before collection.
Scoop sections from water using a loop.
Place the sections on the front side of a silicon wafer.
Dry the sections overnight under a light bulb.
Place the dried silicon wafer on the SEM pin stub using carbon adhesive tape.
Place the sample onto the stub holder suitable for the microscope.
Place the sample into the microscope and wait until a vacuum has been attained before adjusting parameters.
Locate the region of interest under lower magnification mode.
Increase magnification and take individual images.
Maintain EHT at 2 kV, probe current 5–10 pA, and aperture size between 30–60 microns for imaging.
Capture images with a scan speed of 6–9 and resolution of 3072×2304 pixels.
Use line integration mode for noise reduction during image capture.
Process the captured images using ImageJ or Adobe Photoshop.
Pipette out the fixative solution from fixed cells.
Wash the fixed cells three times with 0.1M Na-Cacodylate buffer (pH7.2) for 5 minutes each at room temperature.
Fix the cells with 0.8% Potassium Ferricyanide and 1% Osmium Tetroxide in 0.1M Na-Cacodylate buffer (pH7.2) for 30 minutes on ice.
Wash the fixed cells with 0.1M Na-Cacodylate buffer (pH7.2) three times, each wash lasting five minutes at room temperature.
Wash the fixed cells with distilled water five times, each wash lasting five minutes at room temperature.
Stain the cells with uranyl acetate (UA) in 1% UA and 0.05M Maleate buffer pH5.2 for one hour and thirty minutes at room temperature in the dark.
Transfer the coverslips directly onto a glass petri dish after staining.
Dehydrate the cells using 30% ethanol for seven minutes on ice.
Continue dehydration with 50% ethanol for seven minutes on ice.
Proceed to dehydrate the cells with 70% ethanol for seven minutes on ice.
Pause point: Samples can be stored overnight at step 51c at 4°C if necessary.
Dehydrate the samples using 95% ethanol for seven minutes at room temperature.
Complete dehydration by treating the samples with 100% ethanol three times, each treatment lasting seven minutes at room temperature.
Place the dehydrated coverslips into the pressure chamber of the Leica EM CPD300 Critical Point Dryer instrument.
Fill the pressure chamber with exchange fluid such as ethanol.
Initiate the automatic critical point drying program for human blood cells.
Maintain a constant temperature of 31°C to convert supercritical CO2 to a gaseous state.
Reduce pressure in the chamber by slowly purging the gas at a speed of 20%.
Run the entire program for 3 hours, 8 minutes, and 21 seconds.
Take out the coverslips after the Gas-out phase for sputter coating and imaging.
Place dried coverslips onto an SEM pin stub using carbon adhesive tape on the day of imaging.
Coat the coverslip with gold/palladium at 20-30 mA for 30 seconds in a sputter coater.
Enable stage rotation during coating to achieve a uniform 5-10 nm thick coating.
Place the coated SEM pin stub onto the stub holder suitable for the specific microscope.
Place the sample into the microscope.
Wait until a vacuum has been attained before adjusting parameters.
Locate the region of interest (ROI) under lower magnification mode.
Increase magnification after finding a suitable ROI.
Take individual images in SE mode at 2 kV EHT.
Maintain probe current between 5–10 pA and aperture size between 30 microns.
Capture images with a scan speed of 6–9 and resolution of 2048×1536 pixels.
Use line integration mode for noise reduction.
Process images using ImageJ or Adobe Photoshop.
